summary: TERRA is a one-year Erasmus Mundus master's in earthen architecture and construction, run by the University of Minho, the Technical University of Valencia, ENTPE in Lyon and the University of Florence. Erasmus Mundus scholarships cover the €9,000 fee and pay €1,400 a month, up to €25,800, and consortium scholarships cut the fee for others. The first call closes on 15 January 2027.
meta_title: TERRA 2027: Erasmus Mundus earthen architecture scholarship
meta_description: TERRA covers the €9,000 fee and €1,400 a month for a one-year earthen construction master's in Portugal, Spain, France and Italy. First call 15 January 2027.
covers: Erasmus Mundus scholarship: the €9,000 participation costs, including health insurance, plus €1,400 a month for up to 12 months, worth up to €25,800.
Up to 7 Erasmus Mundus scholarships for students from partner countries such as Ghana and up to 3 for programme countries each year.
Consortium scholarships: up to two of €9,000 (full tuition), four of €6,000 and six of €3,000.
eligibility: A degree in civil engineering, architecture or equivalent: a bachelor's of 240 ECTS, or 300 ECTS (bachelor's plus master's) for tracks that include Florence.
Final-year students can apply if they graduate before 31 July 2027.
English for applicants from non-English-speaking countries: IELTS Academic 6.5, TOEFL iBT 72 or paper 525, or another recognised certificate.
how_to_apply: Apply in the first call, which closes on 15 January 2027. Only the first call awards Erasmus Mundus scholarships.

Upload a motivation letter of 1,500 to 3,500 characters, a Europass CV, diplomas, transcripts with syllabi, English certificates, any work certificates, two recommendation letters (through the portal) and proof of residence issued within the last 12 months.
The top 60 are told by 15 February 2027, interviewed from 22 to 26 February, and receive admission decisions by 5 March 2027.
Later calls close on 15 April and 15 June 2027 for consortium scholarships and self-funded places.
watch_out: A four-year Ghanaian or Nigerian engineering or architecture bachelor's normally gives the 240 ECTS needed; Florence tracks need 300.
Admitted students pay a €250 deposit, refunded when they register at the first university.
On 7 November 2026 the first-call form was marked as opening soon, so check the page in early December.
